images.title: Hui Aloha ʻĀina petition against annexation
images.caption: An original 1897 Hui Aloha ʻĀina petition sheet against annexation, showing the bilingual petition heading and signatures. The National Archives identifies the petition set as carrying 21,269 Native Hawaiian signatures.
images.source_record_label: National Archives, Petition Against the Annexation of Hawaii from Hui Aloha ʻĀina, 1897
images.source_image_access_note: National Archives public-domain educational access image of the original petition sheet.
images.rights_note: Materials created by the National Archives are public domain; the page identifies this as a primary-source petition image.

images.title: Liliʻuokalani protest signatures
images.caption: Signature area from Liliʻuokalani's June 17, 1897 protest against ratification of the annexation treaty, including the Queen's and witness signatures in the UH Mānoa document collection.
images.source_record_label: UH Mānoa Library, Liliʻuokalani to William McKinley, June 17, 1897
images.source_image_access_note: UH Mānoa scan presented with the full protest transcription and document record.
images.rights_note: Historical document scan shown with UH Mānoa provenance; the project links back to the collection record rather than treating the access image as independent authority.

images.title: Hawaiian newspaper printing of Liliʻuokalani's protest
images.caption: A Hawaiian-language newspaper page carrying Liliʻuokalani's June 17 protest. UH Mānoa preserves the newspaper report alongside the signed English protest, making the publication lag visible as an artifact rather than only a note.
images.source_record_label: UH Mānoa Library, Hawaiian-language newspaper report accompanying Liliʻuokalani's June 17, 1897 protest
images.source_image_access_note: UH Mānoa scan of page 1 of the Hawaiian-language newspaper report preserved with the protest collection.
images.rights_note: Historical newspaper scan shown with UH Mānoa provenance and linked to the collection record.

images.title: Hui Pakaka Nalu surf-riding advertisement
images.caption: The exact July 16, 1897 Hui Pakaka Nalu surf-riding advertisement from The Independent, offering first-class canoes with experienced Native canoeists at Waikīkī for $1 per hour per person.
images.source_record_label: The Independent, July 16, 1897, p. 4, SURF RIDING advertisement; Chronicling America
images.source_image_access_note: Secondary web crop of the exact historical advertisement. Chronicling America remains the source authority for the 1897 newspaper page.
images.rights_note: The underlying 1897 newspaper is historical public-domain material; this project preserves the Chronicling America record as authority and identifies the secondary crop only as an access image.

images.title: The Independent, July 1, 1897
images.caption: The exact July 1, 1897 page of The Independent carrying the 'SAVED.' editorial alongside the Mariposa harbor update, the Maunakea Street fire report, and other same-day Honolulu material.
images.source_record_label: The Independent, July 1, 1897, p. 3; Library of Congress Chronicling America
images.source_image_access_note: Library of Congress IIIF image derivative generated directly from the exact NDNP page image. The LOC newspaper record remains source authority.
images.rights_note: The Library of Congress states that newspapers in Chronicling America published more than 95 years ago are in the public domain in their entirety.
